author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A future Earth ruled by genetically superior New Men and telepathic Unusuals is upended when a ninety-thousand-year-old alien intelligence descends to back a human resistance.
page_summary:
Humanity has been stratified: ordinary 'Old Men' are governed by the intellectually enhanced New Men and the psionic Unusuals, who monopolize power and reproduction. Nick Appleton, an ordinary man radicalized by the system, is pulled toward an underground movement whose leader Thors Provoni has gone into deep space seeking help — and returns bringing a colossal, ancient alien organism from the Frolix system to overturn the ruling order.

The novel sets political liberation against a descending savior: a vast intelligence from outside that intervenes in human affairs to break an unjust hierarchy. In his later Exegesis (Lane B), PKD singled out Our Friends from Frolix 8 as one of the few of his novels that portray a genuine 'salvific intervening entity,' reading the Frolixan's arrival as an early fictional sketch of the outside help he came to believe was real. Published in 1970, it closes out the decade with a blunt allegory of caste, resentment, and rescue from above.
